title: A 12-year-old inherited a small chiefdom. By the time he was done, he ruled an empire that stretched from Kabul to Tibet.

sources.text: Sikh Museum UK - Maharaja Ranjit Singh's 235th Birth Anniversary

caption:
A 12-year-old inherited a small chiefdom. By the time he was done, he ruled an empire that stretched from Kabul to Tibet.

He became the leader of a small Sikh chiefdom in Punjab at age 12, after his father's death - and over the following decades, united rival Sikh factions and built the Sikh Empire, one of the last major powers to resist British expansion in the subcontinent.

Ranjit Singh built a modernized, disciplined army trained partly by European officers, ran a famously tolerant administration that included Hindu, Muslim and Sikh officials alike and held off colonial encroachment for his entire 40-year reign.

Ranjit Singh didn't inherit an empire - he built one from a fractured region and ran it as one of the most stable, pluralistic powers of its era.
